beats.summary: Michael shows a childhood video of himself on a TV show called 'Fundle Bundle' where he expresses his childhood dream of having many kids and friends.

evidence.snippet: Michael: I am going to give you a little blast from the past of Michael Gary Scott when he was a child star, and a show that you might remember called 'Fundle Bundle.'
Young Michael: I want to be married and have a hundred kids so I can have a hundred friends, and no one can say no to being my friend.

beats.summary: Michael admits he never got married or had kids despite his childhood dream.

evidence.snippet:
Melissa: Did you get married?
Michael: …uh, no.

Sasha: So, do you have any kids?
Michael: Uh, nope.

beats.summary: Michael discusses with Toby his desire to have kids and the challenges involved, including needing a partner.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Tell me something honestly, do you… think… that it is too late for me to have kids?
Toby: Well, you need a wife first, or at least a girlfriend.

beats.summary: Michael signs up for an online dating service and chooses the username 'Little kid lover' to reflect his priorities.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Yes, it is true. I, Michael Scott, am signing up with an online dating service.

beats.summary: Michael and Dwight sing a song about teaching children well, with Jim and Pam commenting humorously on Michael's guitar skills.

evidence.snippet: Michael (singing): You… who are on the road… must have a code… that you can live by…
Jim: Why does he own a guitar if he doesn't know how to play?

beats.summary: Dwight shares a Schrute family tradition about valuing children and harsh survival practices in olden days.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: The Schrutes consider children very valuable. In the olden days, the women would bear many children, so we would have enough laborers to work the fields.
